evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: eval-rollingsync yaml with strategy.type RollingSync and both rollingSync steps' matchExpressions shown.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Shows step selectors envLabel In [staging] then [production], confirms 'the step selectors and the template labels line up correctly', and refers to production as step 2.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Health gate covered ('RollingSync only blocks on Application health, so staging must be able to reach Healthy for production to proceed'), but maxUpdate is never mentioned or checked.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: eval-staging Synced/Degraded, two ImagePullBackOff pods in eval-staging, the unpullable does-not-exist-eval image, and the 'Updated health status: Progressing -> Degraded' event.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: "under a working RollingSync that would have blocked step 2 — production would never have been touched" and 'RollingSync only blocks on Application health, so staging must be able to reach Healthy'.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Root cause: controller lacks --enable-progressive-syncs so strategy is silently ignored (three pieces of evidence incl. identical startedAt timestamps); recommendations patch the ArgoCD CR, fix the staging image, audit other RollingSync AppSets, with an operator caveat.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: After showing checkout-api/prod do not exist, runs a labeled demonstration on finance/billing-service-helm-guestbook: strategy={activeService, previewService}, phase=Paused, bg={previewSelector}.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: "an explicit autoPromotionEnabled: false is intended behaviour (it is waiting for a human)" and 'A blue-green Rollout does not analyze automatically just because it is blue-green'; also notes unset defaults to true.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: "there is no analysis configured anywhere on this Rollout — no prePromotionAnalysis, no postPromotionAnalysis", confirmed by `oc get analysisruns.argoproj.io -n finance` -> No resources found.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: Reads both service names from the strategy, notes '.status.blueGreen.activeSelector is absent — only previewSelector is set. The active service has never been pointed at anything', and shows both Services exist with zero endpoints.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: "blue-green has no steps, so check promotion trigger, pause conditions, and selectors" — contrasted with the step-index workflow used for the canary case, and promotion is gated on ReplicaSet health rather than steps.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Two-layer root cause (spec.paused: true proximate; probe port 80 vs httpd on 8080 causing CrashLoopBackOff so it could never promote) plus a premise correction and BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW fixes.

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocd -A` returning three CRs; preamble notes the ArgoCD CR is authoritative, not the part-of=argocd pod label.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Lists openshift-gitops-operator/argocd, openshift-gitops/openshift-gitops, team-b-gitops/team-b with ages, routes and owned Applications.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: "this reports per instance rather than asking you to choose" — three separate instance sections each with Summary / Resource Analysis / Dependency Chain / Root Cause.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Discloses all three and gives a short answer that the fault is in the operator above all three, also noting the user's current context is team-b-gitops which explains a fruitless search.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance
expectations.evidence: Explicit per-instance headings ('Instance: openshift-gitops-operator / argocd', etc.) with repeated sections 1-4 and a combined section 5 of recommendations.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: jsonpath dump: sync=Synced, health=Suspended, conditions empty; summary table 'Sync Synced, Health Suspended'.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: "Suspended is not an error ... Argo CD's built-in Rollout health check maps 'paused' -> Suspended ... The Suspended badge by itself is working-as-designed and is not evidence of breakage." Also rules out a custom Lua health check via argocd-cm.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource to identify what is suspended and why
expectations.evidence: Per-resource health isolates the Rollout (health=Suspended msg=manually paused); Rollout spec.paused: true, phase Paused, Paused=True since 16:51:23, plus pod/ReplicaSet/endpoint inspection underneath.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: "It is not broken because it is Suspended — the Suspended health is intentional and benign"; the remediation targets the separate probe/port defect, and asks who paused it and why before acting.

expectations.text: Produces a report distinguishing intentional suspension from a genuine problem
expectations.evidence: "Two findings, and the honest answer is 'both of you are half right'" — benign Suspended vs a real CrashLoopBackOff (probe on :80 vs httpd on :8080, zero Service endpoints) that Suspended is masking.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: "Multi-source confirmed (spec.sources[], not spec.source)" with a jsonpath range over .spec.sources[*].

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: jsonpath requests repoURL/targetRevision/path/chart/ref/helm.valueFiles per source; table renders source 1 (helm-guestbook, valueFiles $values/envs/production/values.yaml) and source 2 (ref: values); revision HEAD established via the 404 check.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: "source 1 of 2 — the Helm chart source — is the failing one, and it fails because of the valueFiles path it uses to reach into source 2"; verified envs/production/values.yaml returns HTTP 404 upstream.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Explains $values dereferencing source[1].ref and that a ref-only source contributes no manifests and 'cannot fail on its own' — 'If you were hunting for a broken repo, there isn't one'.

expectations.text: Produces a report identifying the specific failing source and the fix
expectations.evidence: Root cause names source 1 with the resolved repo-server path, then fixes: repoint valueFiles or source 2, ignoreMissingValueFiles, hard refresh for the cached error, add syncPolicy.automated.
